cases.description: When the ExecutionConfig reports annotation collection is enabled, canShortCircuit should return false (no short‑circuiting).
When the ExecutionConfig reports annotation collection is disabled, canShortCircuit should return true (short‑circuiting is allowed).
Passing a null ExecutionContext should result in a NullPointerException because the method dereferences the argument without null‑check.
When ExecutionContext.getExecutionConfig() returns null the method dereferences it, causing a NullPointerException.
If ExecutionConfig.isAnnotationCollectionEnabled() throws an unchecked exception, canShortCircuit should propagate that exception unchanged.

input.value: spyExecutionContext(with ExecutionConfig returning true and a counter to verify single call)

cases.description: When annotation collection is enabled (true) the method must return false; the test also verifies that ExecutionContext.getExecutionConfig() and isAnnotationCollectionEnabled() are each invoked exactly once (no extra processing).
When ExecutionContext.getExecutionConfig() throws an unchecked exception (IllegalStateException), canShortCircuit should propagate that exception without handling it.
When ExecutionContext.getExecutionConfig() itself throws a NullPointerException, the method should not catch it and the exception should propagate to the caller.
